findings.detail: Not usable English. 'Evite' is an archaic Latinate rarity no learner (and few native speakers) will recognize, and the comma-joined remainder, 'try to make something not appear', is a dictionary paraphrase rather than a gloss. The verb is Austrian/administrative German for preventing or averting something before it can happen (Missbrauch hintanhalten).

The leading synonym 'put back' reads as returning an object to its place, which is zurückstellen or zurücklegen, not this verb; and 'order into a posterior position' is stilted dictionary English. Hintanstellen means to place something last in priority, typically figuratively (seine eigenen Interessen hintanstellen = subordinate one's own interests).

The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first, literal sense (looking over the top of something), while the sense a learner meets is the figurative one at candidate_glosses index 1: über etwas hinwegsehen = to disregard a fault, to turn a blind eye. The English 'look over' also misleads independently, since it usually means to examine.

'Turn upward' describes rotating something so it points up. The verb's everyday sense is increasing a setting by turning: die Heizung/die Musik hochdrehen, and den Motor hochdrehen for revving an engine. English 'turn up' carries exactly that and is what the learner needs.

'Drive upwards/northwards' is kaikki's first-listed sense and the most marginal of the three; the reading a learner actually meets is candidate_glosses index 1, starting up a computer or system (den Rechner hochfahren, die Produktion hochfahren). The slashed 'upwards/northwards' also asks the learner to pick between two unrelated directions.

The importer took kaikki's second, pejorative sense, and 'calculate purposefully high in the dark' is not usable English about anything. Hochrechnen is the neutral statistical verb behind Hochrechnung, the election-night projection: extrapolating a whole from a partial sample. Candidate_glosses index 0 has the right sense ('to project, to cast').

Bare 'hold' presents this as a synonym of halten and invites the learner to write things like 'Ich habe das Buch inne'. Innehaben takes offices, posts, positions, and titles, never physical objects; the restriction is the whole of the word's meaning and candidate_glosses index 0 states it.
